editorial:
Imagine finding out that you almost weren't born. That is exactly where you start with this film. You follow Ash Greyson, a guy who discovers his mother nearly had an abortion right before the law changed. Instead of getting angry or sad, he decides to go on a road trip to find other people who had the same experience. The vibe is surprisingly light and friendly, even though it deals with a topic that usually makes people shout at each other. It feels more like a personal journey than a lecture, and you will feel like you are traveling right along with him as he meets strangers and hears their stories.

What really works here is how the movie avoids using religion or political arguments to make its point. You get real, raw stories from moms and kids that pull at your heartstrings. The pacing is steady, and the emotional honesty keeps you locked in. While it might feel a bit slow in the middle, the payoff is worth it. It is a great pick for anyone who likes documentaries that focus on people rather than politics.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a series of emotional meetings where Ash connects with the people he searched for. You see a beautiful shift from doubt to gratitude as the mothers and children share how their lives turned out. There is no big plot twist, but the real surprise is the sense of peace everyone finds. It ends on a high note, showing that life is a gift and that common ground is possible.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves personal stories and hopeful documentaries.
